journey.title: Escape closes only the innermost open submenu
journey.goal: Escape in the Facts submenu returns to Facts while the About submenu stays open

functionalJourney.title: Open nested submenus with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: About and Facts submenus open on click

guards.title: Escape in a first-level submenu returns to the menubar
guards.goal: Escape in the About submenu closes it and focuses About

plan.root_cause: The Escape key in a submenu was closing all open submenus of the root menu instead of just the current submenu, causing focus to incorrectly return to the menubar item with its aria-expanded set to false.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the Escape key handler in submenus to close only the toggle of the parent menu's current menu item (which opened the current submenu) and then focus the parent menu's current menu item, ensuring only the current submenu closes and focus returns to the correct parent menu item.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape in the Facts submenu will close only the Facts submenu (setting its aria-expanded to false) and return focus to the Facts item, while the About submenu remains open (its aria-expanded stays true).
functional_risks: If the parent menu's currentChild is incorrect due to unrelated bugs, focus may shift to an unintended menu item.

If the parent menu's current menu item is not a submenu item (should not occur when entering a submenu from it), the toggle close is skipped but focus still shifts to the parent menu's current menu item, which is safe but may not be the expected item.
For deeply nested submenus, this change correctly closes only the immediate submenu and returns focus to its parent menu item, preserving the menubar pattern.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape in the Facts submenu (with About submenu open) results in focus on the Facts item (#facts), the Facts submenu's aria-expanded is false, and the About submenu's aria-expanded remains true.
Verify that pressing Escape in the top-level menubar (with no submenu open) still closes the controller if open and focuses the controller.
Verify that pressing Escape in a submenu when the parent menu's current menu item is not a submenu item (if possible) does not cause errors and focuses the parent menu's current menu item.
Verify that pressing Escape in a deeply nested submenu (e.g., three levels) closes only the immediate submenu and returns focus to its parent menu item.

plan.root_cause: The Escape key handler in submenus incorrectly calls rootMenu.closeChildren() which closes all open submenus, and rootMenu.focusCurrentChild() which moves focus to the menubar item instead of the parent submenu item. This causes the About submenu to close and focus to move to About instead of staying on Facts.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the Escape handler in the submenu branch to close only the current submenu via its parent menu item's toggle, then focus the parent menu's current child (the submenu trigger item). This preserves ancestor submenus' open state.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape in the Facts submenu closes only the Facts submenu (aria-expanded becomes false on #facts), returns focus to the Facts menu item (#facts), and leaves the About submenu open (aria-expanded remains true on #about).
functional_risks: If parentMenu.currentChild is stale due to unrelated focus bugs, focus may return to an unexpected sibling item.
If the parent menu's current item is not a submenu item (should not occur when inside a submenu), the toggle close is skipped but focus still moves to the parent menu's current item.
Deeply nested submenus (3+ levels) will correctly close only the immediate submenu and return focus to its direct parent item.
verification_requirements: Verify Escape in Facts submenu (with About open) focuses #facts, sets #facts aria-expanded=false, and #about aria-expanded=true.
Verify Escape in top-level menubar (no submenu open) still closes controller if open and focuses controller.
Verify Escape in a submenu when parent's current item is not a submenu item does not error and focuses parent's current item.
Verify Escape in a three-level nested submenu closes only the innermost submenu and returns focus to its parent item.
